doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Closing: Billie's sister Sadie and other sisters
summary: Billie says Sadie played with Tuxedo, Celestin, Buddy Petit and Ike Morgan, and that Edna and the younger sisters only visited New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: St. Claude. I can't call that man's name too. name right. He and Chippard lived almost in the sand block at one time. We'll run across the name someplace. I'm trying to say that but I know it's good. I know the boy's good. He's working with me. You? I can't call the boy's name. Just about a minute left on here. Can you think of anything else about your life you'd like to tell or the old bands that you've played with? Either one of you? I'm more clear than I've told you before. I think you've covered everything pretty well. Anything about your sisters though since I don't know them and may not see them, Billy? That you could tell? Sadie, who she played with? You said she played at Piku, different ones there.
She played with Tuxedo and Papa Celestan. She played with Papa Celestan and Buddy P.T. The one I know, she played with Ike Morgan. She played with them.
Well that's quite a few of them. Your other sister Edna that was older, did she play with bands here in town much?

Well she had no, no she didn't play. She just worked with Diddy and her and her husband. See, they just come over here for a visit. She traveled show business all the time. She didn't stay in New Orleans. No, she didn't stay long. So she went to the Cadden Field out there a long time with Diddy until they got ready to see the old brother go back on the show, you see. They went back on the show. Any of your younger sisters work over here in New Orleans? No, she just come over here and visit. That's all. She never work here. She just run in and run out. Sadie was here quite a while. Sadie was here for years. We may get to see her someday I hope. Yeah, I hope so too.

Well, any chance that she'd be back for a visit? I sure would. You know, I don't know. She may come. She never tell, you know. She never tell. She might make up her mind to come here. I don't know if she came down every year or very often or anything like that.

No, Sadie hadn't been back to New Orleans since she left. That's where she left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left. She left.
